AfterBlockCleared.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The arithmetic, the turn index, the target test and the ValueProp all match; what diverges is that the sim only FIRES the hook when a block clear actually happened, so a turn-3 block-clear preventer silences the relic.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): C#'s AfterBlockCleared is a separate UNCONDITIONAL loop; the sim fires on_block_cleared only inside the `if should_clear_block(...)` arm
guards.rationale: The divergence this guard names -- on_block_cleared fired only inside the `if should_clear_block(...)` arm -- no longer exists. sts2_rl/player.py:169-175 reproduces C#'s two-loop structure: CombatManager.cs:492-499 runs `foreach (Creature item3 in creaturesStartingTurn) await item3.AfterTurnStart(_state.CurrentSide);` and CombatManager.cs:500-507 then runs a SEPARATE `foreach (Creature item4 in creaturesStartingTurn) await Hook.AfterBlockCleared(_state, item4);` with no condition attached. The sim's player.py:175 and combat.py:363 are that second loop: unconditional, outside the if/else, and (on the player side) outside the `if not self._first_turn:` early-return that mirrors Creature.cs:681-692. Captain's Wheel maps 1:1 -- CaptainsWheel.cs:20-27 `AfterBlockCleared(Creature creature)` with `creature == base.Owner.Creature && base.Owner.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber == 3` then CreatureCmd.GainBlock(18, Unpowered) vs sts2_rl/relics/captains_wheel.py:19-22 `on_block_cleared` with `target is self.player and self.turn == 3` then BlockCmd.apply(..., 18, props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED). Executed with the ported preventer (relics/sturdy_clamp.py:23-25) held, the sim now grants the 18 the game grants.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: This is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json guard G1 (step 14) at the site that record already names, and one verdict per mechanism (binding rule 3) means it is cited rather than re-derived. C# runs two separate loops over the same participants -- AfterTurnStart/ClearBlock (CombatManager.cs:492-499), then `Hook.AfterBlockCleared` for EVERY participant (500-507) -- so the event fires for a creature with no block, for a creature whose clear a ShouldClearBlock listener prevented, and for a player on turn 1 whose AfterTurnStart returned early. player.py:157-159 fuses them. LIVE, and the seam's own executed numbers are this relic's: '[captains_wheel] reaches turn 3 with 18 block, [sturdy_clamp, captains_wheel] with 0' -- C# gives 18 in both cases. The preventers are ported content (BarricadePower via the Ironclad Rare card cards/barricade_card.py, and relic/sturdy_clamp), Captain's Wheel is Rare in the transcribed grab bag (confirmed by `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3-pool`), and turn 3 is reached in most fights. The seam owns the machinery; this record owns the relic's observable. Pinned there by test_hook_order.py::TestTurnStructureOrder::test_block_clear_event_fires_even_when_prevented.

Same test. It is load-bearing rather than incidental: the sim fires on_block_cleared for enemies too (combat.py:296-298), so without the identity check the relic would grant the player block on every enemy's turn-3 clear.
audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json's extra-turn step names Captain's Wheel by name as one of the ported TurnNumber readers that self.turn correctly models. Cited, not re-derived (binding rule 3).

guards.what: N3: `BlockVar(18m, ValueProp.Unpowered)` passed whole to CreatureCmd.GainBlock (CaptainsWheel.cs:16, 25) vs `BlockCmd.apply(..., 18, props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED)` (captains_wheel.py:22)
guards.rationale: 18 on both sides with no AscensionHelper call in the file, and the Unpowered prop rides along in both. The prop matters: BlockCmd.apply (cmds.py:131-152) skips modify_block_additive/multiplicative unless `is_powered_attack(props)`, so Dexterity and Frail do NOT scale the 18 -- which is what ValueProp.Unpowered means in the game. The third argument is the card source, null on both sides.

guards.what: N4: the sim's on_block_cleared slot vs C#'s step 14
guards.rationale: Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order`): on_block_cleared fires first in the turn, before on_energy_reset and before the draw, matching step 14's position between ClearBlock (12) and the energy reset (17). So the 18 Block is present for the whole of turn 3, including anything that reads player block during turn setup -- the slot that relic/anchor's N3 records as WRONG in the sim is a different hook, not this one.
